name: Foreman's Blackjack
summary: Foreman's Blackjack keeps peons at work in Durotar's Valley of Trials. Foremen use the leather-wrapped cosh to wake laborers who fall asleep during the Horde's early construction.

sections.title: A Tool of Orcish Labor
sections.body: Durotar's rugged desert needs stockpiles of lumber for the Horde's new home. In the Valley of Trials, the work falls to the peons, and Foreman Thazz'ril keeps the crews moving with Foreman's Blackjack. The weighted bludgeon delivers a jarring wake-up call to laborers caught napping beneath the valley's shade trees, rather than a lethal blow. Peon life in the new Horde means grueling, unglamorous work under an iron fist.

faq.q: What is the Foreman's Blackjack used for?
faq.answer: Overseers give the blackjack to young adventurers to discipline sleeping peons in the Valley of Trials. A strike jolts a napping peon awake and sends them straight back to chopping and hauling wood.
Foreman Thazz'ril owns the blackjack. The labor taskmaster is stationed in the Valley of Trials, where he oversees the collection of raw timber for the young Orc settlement.

faq.q: Why do the peons keep falling asleep on the job?
faq.answer: Orcish peons work relentless, exhausting shifts gathering wood under Durotar's harsh sun. They often nap without permission beneath the valley's sparse trees when exhaustion overtakes them.

faq.q: Can I keep the blackjack after finishing the task?
faq.answer: No. The overseer demands the tool back immediately after the shirkers have been disciplined. It stays on hand for taskmasters enforcing labor quotas.

angles.text: For young orcs entering the Valley of Trials, wielding the blackjack offers an early lesson in Horde hierarchy: those without a warrior's strength or spirit are relegated to labor and kept in line by force.
The blackjack reflects the practical effort needed to tame Durotar, where settling a harsh land requires every laborer to work without pause.
